questions.q: What distinguishes wide data from long data?
options: Wide data spreads categories or time periods across separate columns; long data puts every observation in its own row with the category/period as a value in one column
Wide data has more rows than long data
Wide data can only contain numbers; long data can only contain text
There is no real difference — the terms are interchangeable
questions.explain: Wide data uses column names like Jan/Feb/Mar as if they were separate fields; long data has one Month column whose values are Jan, Feb, Mar.

questions.q: Why does Tableau specifically prefer long data over wide data?
options: Tableau treats each column as one field you can drag onto a shelf or filter — wide data splits what should be one dimension (like Month) into several unrelated fields
Tableau cannot open wide spreadsheets at all
Long data always loads faster regardless of size
Wide data is against Tableau's licensing terms
questions.explain: Tableau's model assumes each field is one draggable thing. Wide data with separate Jan/Feb/Mar columns has no single Month field to use as a real time dimension.

questions.q: How can you tell a dataset is wide just by looking at its column headers?
options: Category or date values themselves (like Jan, Feb, Mar, or 2022, 2023) appear as column names, instead of as values within a single column
Wide data always has fewer than 5 columns
Wide data column headers are always in all capital letters
There is no reliable way to tell from column headers alone
questions.explain: When category or period values show up as column names themselves, that's the signature of wide data — a long dataset would have a single 'Month' or 'Year' column instead.

questions.q: According to this lesson, why does the Sample Superstore dataset arrive already long?
options: It was built to be Tableau-ready from the start — one row per order line, with Order Date as a single column
It has no dates in it at all
It was originally wide and had to be manually reshaped by every student
Long format is required by Excel, not Tableau
questions.explain: Sample Superstore's one-row-per-order-line structure with a single Order Date column is exactly the long shape Tableau wants — no reshaping needed before connecting.

questions.q: What tool, introduced in the previous lesson, can reshape a wide dataset into long format directly inside Tableau?
options: Pivot (part of Tableau's Data Interpreter / data-cleaning tools)
The Marks card
A calculated field
The Analytics pane
questions.explain: Tableau's Pivot tool, covered in Lesson 12's data-cleaning content, reshapes wide columns into a single long field pair without needing an external tool first.
